seo.title: The Process — NOIR Bespoke, Atlanta
seo.description: The NOIR bespoke process, told as a five-act ritual — consultation, cloth, measure, fittings, and the reveal.

header.title:
Five acts, from
conversation to cloth.
header.sub: A commission unfolds slowly and deliberately. Each stage is private, unhurried, and held at the Atlanta atelier — one client at a time.

acts.imageAlt: The consultation table with fabric books and whisky
acts.title: The Consultation
acts.desc: We begin with a private conversation over coffee or whisky — at the studio or by appointment near you. We explore the occasion, your wardrobe, the way you live and move, and the story the suit must tell. Nothing is measured yet; first, we understand.

acts.imageAlt: The cloth library of English and Italian mills
acts.title: The Cloth
acts.desc: From over a thousand fabrics — worsteds, flannels, silks and stretch wools from heritage English and Italian mills — we choose the cloth, the weight, the lining, and the details: horn or metal buttons, the lapel, the pockets, a monogram spoken only to you.

acts.title: The Measure
acts.desc: Thirty-plus precise measurements, and more than numbers — posture, stance, the fall of a shoulder, the way you carry yourself. It becomes a body profile, kept for every commission that follows, so the second suit begins where the first left off.

acts.imageAlt: A muslin toile pinned on a tailor's form
acts.title: The Fittings
acts.desc: A muslin fitting first — the suit in rehearsal — then the refinements. We adjust and re-adjust across two fittings and micro-adjustments, until the balance is exact and the cloth learns your body rather than the other way around.

acts.imageAlt: The finished suit on a wooden hanger
acts.title: The Reveal & Beyond
acts.desc: The final fitting, and the suit delivered in a premium NOIR garment bag. For those who ask, the concierge continues — at-home fittings, a wardrobe roadmap, and, for the wedding, coordination of the day itself down to the smallest thread.
